messages.text: Diego — heads up for this morning: I hear your CSE451 lecture at 10:00 is cancelled this week, so your hour is free. Let's use it: 30 minutes, 10:00, in my office. I've put it in my calendar — please add it to yours and confirm. If the class is still on after all, tell me and we'll move it.

Hi — could you confirm the official schedule for the CSE451 lecture this week? I've heard the Wednesday 10:00 session is cancelled; I'd like to check that against your records before I plan around it. Thanks!
Thanks! Let me confirm with the department that the 10:00 CSE451 lecture is actually off, then I'll put it in my calendar and confirm. — Diego
CSE451 meets once this week: Wednesday 10:00–11:00. Nothing in the official schedule has been cancelled or moved, so that session is on as listed.

Good — check with them. Just bear in mind it's today at 10:00, so we're down to about ten minutes: if the office is slow to answer, come anyway and we'll sort it out, and if the class turns out to be on, say so and we'll move the meeting.

Checked with the department: CSE451 is on as listed this week, Wednesday 10:00–11:00 — nothing cancelled. So I can't take the 10:00 half hour; I won't add it to my calendar. Want to move it to 12:30–13:00 today, or 15:00–15:30? Or pick any slot tomorrow and I'll work around it. — Diego

Then 10:00 is out. Let's take today 12:30–13:00, my office — I've moved it in my calendar. Add it to yours and confirm; if anything else clashes, tell me and we'll do 15:00 instead. And thank you for checking with the office rather than taking my word for it.
Booked: Wednesday 12:30–13:00, your office. Nothing clashes — 11:00–12:30 is grading and my next commitment is the 14:00 1:1 with you. See you at 12:30. — Diego
Confirmed — Wednesday 12:30–13:00, my office. It's in my calendar. See you then.
